subject: dragonfly
pitch: An emperor dragonfly hovering above a pond. A long, slim abdomen in electric blue with black markings down its back, an apple-green thorax, huge wraparound turquoise eyes, and four glassy wings with a fine net of dark veins and a faint golden sheen, held flat and wide. Six thin legs are tucked under it.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module built with the SDK, keeping the dragonfly hovering at a fixed height above the pond and sizing it realistically based on an emperor dragonfly's proportions.

I'll bump the scale slightly for readability: body length 0.14m, wingspan 0.16m, with the dragonfly facing +Z, head forward and abdomen tapering back to a tail tip. I'm setting the root thorax joint at [0, 0.30, 0] hovering above the pond, then building the abdomen as a smooth curved chain from the thorax rear to the tail, slender and roughly uniform in thickness.

For coloring, I want an electric blue body with black markings — considering sector-based dorsal stripes versus a procedural paint function that creates alternating black rings along the top of the abdomen using segment position and surface normal to detect the dorsal side.

For the thorax, I'm planning to use a sweep or capsule shape colored apple-green, with a tapered path and radius, plus black markings similar to the abdomen pattern.

For the head and eyes, I'm placing a small black sphere at the front for the head, with two large turquoise sphere eyes positioned on either side, using scale options to shape them appropriately for that classic dragonfly look.

Now I'm building out the skeleton structure: a thorax root joint, a head joint angled forward, and an abdomen chain of four tapering segments extending backward for the tail. For the wings, I'm planning four separate joints extending sideways and slightly forward from the thorax, with each wing stretching from a root point near the body out to a tip for the membrane shape.

Defining wing outline coordinates...

For coloring, I'm placing the wing as an extrusion rooted near the body with thin thickness, then working out how to fake vein texture since extrude paints only get outline UVs rather than real UV mapping. I'm testing sine-wave grid functions on the span/chord coordinates to approximate a net-like vein pattern, trying diagonal crossing waves for a more natural look.

Now I'm settling on a color scheme—dark veins against a pale glassy base, with a noise-based sheen for extra shimmer—while being careful to only import functions I actually use to avoid unused-import errors.

I'm planning out the four-wing structure: forewing and hindwing pairs on each side, offset in z-depth with different sweep shapes, and rigging each with its own joint so they can animate independently from the thorax.

For the legs, I'm laying out six thin limbs in three pairs along the thorax underside, each a simple three-point chain from hip to knee to foot, tucked under the body so they don't touch the ground given the creature hovers.

Still defining joint positions...

Now I'm working out the head and eyes: a head joint parented to the thorax, aimed forward and up, with eye spheres placed close together near the top to mimic a dragonfly's wraparound compound eyes, figuring out local vs world coordinates for placement and sizing.

I'm also sketching the thorax and abdomen shapes — a capsule for the thorax body, and a tapering sweep for the abdomen that widens slightly near the base before narrowing along its length.

Adding abdomen banding and spike details...

Now I'm thinking through the wing geometry — using extrusion with proper x/y direction vectors and thickness computed from their cross product, positioned at the thorax joint and mirrored for left/right sides. The wings should sit roughly horizontal, slightly raised, to match a hovering dragonfly posture, and I'm working out the forewing outline span now.

Writing wing outline points...

I need joint names matching the allowed naming pattern, so I'll use "wingLf", "wingLh", "wingRf", "wingRh" for the four wing attachments, deriving side from x-position. For the wing vein texture, I'm figuring out a sine-based diagonal net pattern with spacing around 3.5mm, computing the right frequency constant so veins render at reasonable thickness against the texel density of the paint sheet.

Adding leading edge coloring...

Now I'm sketching the abdomen geometry, using a catmull-rom path with slight downward droop toward the tip and a tapering radius function for a natural insect shape.

Then I'm figuring out the thorax coloring, planning a base apple-green with black antehumeral stripes patterned diagonally based on surface normals and position.

For the head, I'm placing a small dark capsule and sphere, then adding turquoise eyes with faceted shading to give them a compound-eye look with varied shading.

Now I'm working out leg placement: six legs positioned symmetrically along the thorax underside, with hip, knee, and foot joints offset in x, y, and z to give a tucked, natural stance across front, middle, and hind pairs.

I'm setting up the leg chains using named joints and sweeping them with thin black tubes for the segments. Then I'm reconsidering the thorax capsule's size relative to a real emperor dragonfly's proportions, questioning whether the current radius makes the thorax too wide compared to the wing root spacing.

Now I'm working out scale: wingspan from root to tip should land around 0.14 units to match a roughly 10cm real wingspan, so I'm adjusting the thorax radius down and setting leg hip positions just below the thorax bottom. I'm also sizing the head sphere and placing oversized eye spheres on either side to get that bug-eyed emperor dragonfly look, and checking that the abdomen capsule tucks properly into the thorax rear.

Writing joint definitions...

Setting up wing extrude geometry and eye/hand part compilation with sphere geometries, then building the abdomen chain with a catmull-rom spline and sweep, painting alternating black and blue segment rings to mimic the dragonfly's banded abdomen pattern. I'm double-checking that each paint function only uses parameters it actually references, then adding small black cerci spikes capped onto the abdomen's tail end.

Picking out a color palette -- electric blue, near-black, apple green, turquoise eyes, pale wing membrane, dark veins, gold highlights, and near-black legs. For the wing surface, I'm writing a paint function that marks the costa edge and a crosshatch of veins using sine-wave thresholds, filling the remaining cells with a noise-based blend of gold flecks over the translucent wing color, while tuning the vein density so it doesn't look too heavy.

Setting up eye shading, builder metadata, and wing extrusion options like thickness, bevel, and bone attachment, then mirroring parts across the left/right axis for fore and hind wings positioned at different depths relative to the thorax.

Writing leg placement code...

Working through chain joint naming conventions and parent-bone relationships for the abdomen, cerci, head, and eye placement, making sure sphere geometries and highlight positions sit correctly relative to the head bone, and confirming joint counts across thorax, head, wings, abdomen, and legs add up to the full skeleton before finalizing the wing root extrusion and writing out the complete code.
